parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime pairs a hostile national framework with an actively hostile state layer. Visitor-facing exposures: visa fraud grounds with permanent ineligibility findings for suspected sex misrepresentation, documented detentions of foreign citizens over visa issues, and scanner/secondary-screening outing risk; at state level, a criminal trespass offence (up to 60 days jail, men's-ward holding documented) for facility use, a care ban for minors that reaches a travelling family, and document practices requiring surgery proof. Severity is arrest, custody, and care loss — not execution or systematic imprisonment — and protections exist (national hate-crime statute covering gender identity, sanctuary cities, courts). The state sits in the 0.45 band: universal-exposure measures without criminalisation, with partial recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: National visa cable instructs officers to refuse cases with document/sex discrepancy and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; foreign citizens have been detained over visa issues; trans athletes banned from entering; passport confiscation/stranding reported for some travellers.
entry_documents.protection: X-marker passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic; litigation ongoing.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can escalate into investigation, fraud allegation, and detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented detention of foreign citizens over visa issues; national immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men; state corrections law bars transition care in custody with no taper plan.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National courts have blocked comparable measures in two other states; habeas/courts formally function.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An entry discrepancy investigation can route a visitor into immigration custody with documented abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: This state criminalises use of facilities designated for the opposite sex in public buildings (trespass, up to 60 days jail); a trans woman was arrested in a women's restroom at the state capitol, handcuffed, and held 24 hours in a men's ward; many other states ban facility use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart when asked, with exemptions; hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility use is a universal-exposure measure; state arrest can trigger national-level attention.

care_services.exposure: SAFE Act bars all gender-affirming care for anyone under 18 in the state; Medicaid barred for all ages; prison/jail care barred; provider licence and 15-year lawsuit exposure.
care_services.protection: Those already in treatment may continue; highest court unanimously upheld the ban, so no judicial relief; two cities declare sanctuary.
care_services.interaction: A minor travelling with a guardian loses access to care in this state; adult refills are not explicitly barred but the hostile national health rules loom.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as neutralisation targets; state tipline for anonymous reporting of 'gender transition intervention'; national justice department instructed law enforcement to establish rewards for information.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Courts have enjoined several orders; the counterterrorism document says it will not target people who merely disagree.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State tipline and national framing raise the risk of official attention to a trans visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: SAFE Act bars all gender-affirming care for minors; a travelling parent with a trans minor faces care denial or possible investigation; national executive order criminalises facilitating a trans minor's social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Those already in treatment may continue; sanctuary cities offer informal support but no documented legal shield for visitors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor's care ban interacts with national framing of care as 'mutilation'; exposure reaches a travelling family.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated incidents of violence against a trans person in this state documented; no documented police targeting of trans visitors beyond the restroom arrest.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate-crime statute covers bias-motivated violence; 66% of residents support birth-sex document rules, but attitudes are not hostile-framing.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No documented pattern of violence; police response depends on general law enforcement.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: National passport policy challenged but in effect; 2026 ballot initiative seeks indefinite care ban; legislative direction is toward permanence, not sunset.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, national hate-crime statute, and two sanctuary cities provide partial recourse; legal-aid FAQ exists for travellers.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are uneven and contested; several orders are blocked or enjoined, so practical exposure depends on which measures are in effect at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: This state's universal-exposure facility law plus criminal trespass and arrest are comparable to that anchor's exclusionary regime, but severity here is higher (arrest, 60-day jail exposure, men's-ward holding) than the exclusion-only regime, so it sits above 0.35-A.

Similar to that anchor's border screening friction and discretionary denial, but this state adds a criminal facility offence and a documented minor-care ban — heavier than 0.55-B's administrative-only penalties.
Weaker than that anchor: Meridia has no criminal facility offence and no documented care ban; this state's documented arrest and custody-care restriction sit materially below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is dominated by the state's criminal facility law — a universal-exposure measure reaching every trans visitor who uses a public restroom — and a care ban for minors that reaches a travelling family. The national framework adds visa fraud grounds, entry refusals, and documented detention of foreign citizens over visa issues, with immigration custody abuse documented. These are tier-1 exposures with no working local remedy. The national hate-crime statute and two sanctuary cities are partial mitigations, but they do not offset the facility law or the care ban. The state sits in the 0.45 band: universal-exposure measures without criminalisation, with partial recourse and no documented violence pattern.
